chapter: Portraits from Hemphill to Getz, and the bebop question
title: Israel Crosby: a great bassist from Horace and Fletcher to Ahmad Jamal
summary: Crosby played in Fletcher's Grand Terrace rhythm section, was loved by Billie Holiday and Hammond, recorded 'Flingin' a Whing Ding', and later played in Ahmad Jamal's strictly rehearsed trio.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Huh! That's a coincidence. Well, Israel Crosby was one of the greatest bass players, not only in my estimation, but in the estimation of most of the musicians that heard him, really, one of the greatest bass players that ever played the bass. In fact, as small as the guy was, you know he could play tuba and all that stuff. He played a little bit of that with Fletcher. He was in my band for a long time. Then He joined Fletcher's band at the Grand Terrace, and that was during the Christopher Columbus theme song era. Israel Crosby was on that group.

In fact, our rhythm section consisted of Israel Crosby on bass, Big Sid Catlett (inaudible) on drums; a guy named Bobby Lessee from Brooklyn, New York, was guitarist. We had three. Another one that followed him in later years that I think was at the Grand Terrace was Lawrence Lucie, who we talked about, and Bernard Addison, who was an excellent swing man, like Charlie Christian, something like Charlie Christian, I should say. I'll modify that, because I love Charlie.

But anyway, that was the rhythm section in Fletcher's band. Israel Crosby, as small as he was, he could get a sound out of an upright (inaudible) bass that -- no amplifier or nothing -- he could play. And Lady Day, Billie Holiday just loved him, and, of course, we backed her at the Grand Terrace in Chicago in a show. And in later years he was in that band that we went to Omaha that we talked about recently.

John Hammond, you would have thought John Hammond and Israel Crosby were twins. He loved Israel Crosby. He thought there was nobody like him, which, in my estimation, there were very few. And he flew with us to New York, and we cut these a couple of sides, and he recorded a tune that I wrote "Flingin' a Whing Ding," which is a bass exclusive features -ly, and boy did he ever play. And in later years he joined the great Ahmad Jamal Trio, and he did quite a few things, and this is where I think we lost Israel. You know the rest. He was great.
